beats.narration: The application lands in the Onboarding inbox: release $15,000 on severe financial hardship grounds, with a Services Australia letter and overdue notices attached.
Olivia's agent extracts the application and the Services Australia letter dated Mon 9 Nov 2026 — JobSeeker paid continuously since 6 April 2026.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261111-OPS004, flags Tom as a vulnerable member, and routes it to Benefits & Eligibility.
Ben checks the severe financial hardship criteria and payment limits in the SIS Regulations and the trust deed.
Ben: 31 weeks of income support (26 needed) ✓, still receiving ✓, letter within 21 days ✓, no release in the last 12 months ✓ — but $10,000 is the legal maximum, so he recommends a partial approval.
Theo personally reviews the vulnerable-member case and approves a partial release of $10,000 gross.
Ivy plans the redemption — drawn from cash first, then Balanced model units — to keep selling to a minimum.
Ben hands the approved partial release to Payments.
Penny matches the payee name and BSB ✓ and splits the $10,000: tax-free $600, taxable $9,400, PAYG withheld $2,068 (22%) — $7,932 paid on Fri 13 Nov 2026.

Cara sends Tom a kind, plain-English letter: why $10,000 is the legal maximum, the tax, the impact on his retirement savings, and free help from the National Debt Helpline (1800 007 007) and Moneysmart.

result.headline: Partially approved — $10,000 legal maximum
result.summary: Outcome: PARTIALLY APPROVED — $10,000 gross of the $15,000 requested; $7,932 paid after $2,068 PAYG withholding
